result.dimension: PARAMETER PROVENANCE + PI-GAP INVENTORY — what is blocked on a number
result.summary: The `ac/engine` layer has genuinely excellent source-gating discipline — `_require_param` / `_GAP_PARAMS` (cortex_motor_slice.py:167-215), `ERMBellKinetics` (erm_cortex_connector.py:174-177), `RestingBoundMyosinSetpoint`, `NonlinearCableCard`, `DynamicInstabilityRateCard(ratified=False)`, `build_sf_mechanics_topology` and the `--k-axial required=True` CLIs all refuse to invent a magnitude. But the engine is not where the banked GATE-A/GATE-B numbers came from: the running incumbent `ac/cell/assemble.py` **silently defaults the entire NMII force-scale** (lines 142-155 → injected into live `NMIIHandParams` at 575-584 and into the resting-seed plan at 828) and `ac/cell/compartments.py:101-121` silently defaults the whole nucleus/LINC GAP set, including `eps_rupture=0.50` which its own parameter gate (`ac/nucleus/params_i0b2.yaml:145`) explicitly says "do NOT keep ff proxy 0.50". Turgor `PI_0_PA = 40.0` (assemble.py:128) has no guard, no provenance latch, is a HeLa proxy below the entire MCF7 range, and is simultaneously used as ΔP_hyd *and* ΔΠ_osm (driver.py:1057 — a conflation the yaml itself flags). The ERM areal density — the sole cortex→membrane load path — is not a parameter at all in any banked run: it is `n_erm = n_verts`, so it swings from ~58/µm² (subdiv 6, all GATE-A/B scripts) to ~927/µm² (subdiv 8, the PI-ratified "production RESTING" config), i.e. a physical density set by a numerical knob and ~9× off the sourced Alert baseline. The PI-GAP card inventory is also stale in both directions: it over-declares two gaps that are already sourced in-tree (S1 EA_actin — `ff/kim_network.py:35` Kojima 1994, KB verdict **OK**; F2 fascin spacing — `ac/engine/protrusion.py:269` Courson 2010), and omits ~7 declared `params_i0b3` GAPs plus the three cortex-geometry convenience values its own companion audit ranked worst. Worst citation finding: the ONE branch-angle set declared "verified/High … the ONLY admissible constants" traces to `Fassler2020_EMBOJ`, whose `source_audit` verdict is **DOI_DEAD**, and Billington2013 / Freedman2017 / Tam2021 / Stam2015 / Veigel2003 / Hill1938 / Alert2016 / Tseng2004 are all **CHECK**, Dejardin2020 **DOI_MISMATCH**, Pereverzev2005 **NO_DOI_FOUND** — while Rusan, Courson, Qin, Lichtenstern, Lin 2010, Jung 2011, Morone, Lorenz have **no audit row at all**.

claims.claim: The entire NMII force-scale PI-GAP set is SILENTLY DEFAULTED in the running incumbent `ac/cell` build and injected into the live device motor params — not merely 'unused while unbound'. `NMII_K_XB_TEST=1.0e3`, `NMII_F_STALL_TEST=0.5`, `NMII_V0_TEST=0.12`, `NMII_KAPPA_TEST=0.5`, `NMII_KON_TEST=50.0`, `NMII_N_SIDE=10`, `NMII_HEAD_OFFSET_UM=0.200`, `NMII_L_BB_UM=0.301` are module constants with no guard, and `_build_myosin` writes them straight into `NMIIHandParams`.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:142-155 (constants, each annotated '(GAP)'); assemble.py:575-584 `params.k_on = wp.float64(NMII_KON_TEST) … params.k_xb = wp.float64(NMII_K_XB_TEST) … params.capture_radius = wp.float64(NMII_CAPTURE_UM)`; assemble.py:601 `k_theta_arm = arm_orientation_k_theta(NMII_K_XB_TEST, NMII_HEAD_OFFSET_UM)`. Contrast the engine, which refuses: ac/engine/cortex_motor_slice.py:167-175 `_GAP_PARAMS = frozenset({"k_on","f_stall","v0","kappa","k_xb","r0_head","k_catch0","x_catch","k_slip0","x_slip"})` + `_require_param` raising 'REQUIRED-PARAM … (KB/PI GAP — source it or surface to PI, never default)'.

claims.claim: The resting bound-myosin setpoint is only PARTIALLY source-gated: `RestingBoundMyosinSetpoint` mandates `fraction` + `per_head_force_pn` + a source string, but the crossbridge stiffness that converts the requested force into a seeded abscissa is silently taken from the GAP constant `NMII_K_XB_TEST`. So the 'source-gated' resting mechanism still runs on an unsourced master knob.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:828 `plan_resting_bound_heads(..., k_xb=float(NMII_K_XB_TEST), r0_xb=0.0, capture_radius_um=capture_um)` and assemble.py:832 `resting_tangential_load_reference(..., k_xb=float(NMII_K_XB_TEST), ...)`; the gated fields are ac/motor/resting_setpoint.py:62-92 (`fraction`, `per_head_force_pn`, `source` all validated, no default).

claims.claim: The GATE-B 'tension EMERGES from binding events' native result — the headline dynamic-slice claim — rests entirely on four hardcoded, admittedly-unsourced Pereverzev constants plus the silently-defaulted k_xb. The catch-slip constants are mandatory when `detach_kinetics == CATCH_SLIP` (the physiological default), and the only supplier is a script-level literal.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:114-120 `# PROVISIONAL catch-slip constants (Pereverzev two-pathway) — NOT SOURCED, PI/KB GAP` … `CATCH_SLIP_PROVISIONAL = dict(k_catch0=0.35, x_catch=1.0e-3, k_slip0=0.35, x_slip=0.6e-3)`; consumed at :167; the required-ness is ac/engine/cortex_motor_slice.py:224-226. Note k_catch0 == k_slip0 == 0.35 is a symmetric placeholder, not a fit.

claims.claim: Turgor Π₀ = 40 Pa — the single most load-bearing baseline (γ_total = ΔP·R/2) — is a bare module constant with NO required-param guard, NO provenance latch, and NO GAP marker in code. It is a Fischer-Friedrich HeLa proxy that implies γ_total = 0.15 mN/m, BELOW the entire MCF7 Hosseini IQR (0.18–0.40), i.e. ~45% under the MCF7 central 72 Pa. Every GATE-A/GATE-B magnitude inherits it.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:128 `PI_0_PA = 40.0  # resting osmotic turgor Π₀ [Pa]` (no guard; compare the erm_* / resting_* fields at assemble.py:252-284 which ARE latched to `None` + a source string). Consumed at assemble.py:917,963,971; driver.py:1057; bleb_growth.py:185; dump_state.py:91. Derivation of 72 Pa (48–107) in docs/v2_audit/TURGOR_PRESSURE_MCF7_2026-07-24.md §3.

claims.claim: One scalar is used for two physically distinct quantities: the net hydrostatic ΔP_hyd the cortex bears and the osmotic ΔΠ_osm that drives water flux. The fluid parameter gate names this as a defect; the driver still does it.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/cell/driver.py:1057 `osmotic_difference=lambda t: PI_0_PA,   # resting osmotic balance ⇒ zero net membrane flux`; the flag is ac/fluid/params_i0b1.yaml:174-177 'Do NOT reuse one scalar for both (the current driver osmotic_difference=PI_0_PA conflates them — flagged for separation).' Inert at rest (ΔΠ=ΔP ⇒ zero flux) but wrong the moment anything perturbs.

claims.claim: ERM areal density ρ₀ is not a parameter in any banked run: `erm_density_per_um2` defaults to None, which selects a one-tether-per-membrane-vertex topology explicitly labelled DIAGNOSTIC, so the physical linker density is fixed by `membrane_subdivisions`. No GATE-A or GATE-B script ever sets a density. That means ~58/µm² at the subdiv-6 gate runs and ~927/µm² at the PI-ratified subdiv-8 'production RESTING' config (655,362 verts / 706.86 µm²) — a 16× swing on the SOLE cortex→membrane load path, and ~9× above the sourced Alert baseline ρ₀≈100/µm².
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:250-254 (`erm_density_per_um2: float | None = None`); ac/cell/compartments.py:650-668 `if density is None: … pairing_mode = "RADIAL_ONE_PER_MEMBRANE_NODE_DIAGNOSTIC"` / `"UNSOURCED_ONE_PER_MEMBRANE_NODE_DIAGNOSTIC"`; assemble.py:230-244 comment concedes '(n_erm=n_verts)' and even labels subdiv-7's 235/µm² 'physiological' with no source; grep of scripts/ac_gate_a*.py + ac_gate_b*.py shows `erm_radial_pairing=True, membrane_subdivisions=6|8` and ZERO `erm_density_per_um2=` occurrences.

claims.claim: The nucleus/LINC PI-GAP set is silently defaulted at TEST values through a plain dict with no guard, in direct contradiction of the parameter gate that owns them. `ac/nucleus/params_i0b2.yaml` sets `eps_rupture: null  # GAP — do NOT choose; do NOT keep ff proxy 0.50` and `k_linc: null  # HALT -> PI (no Hookean k exists)` and `lamin_AC_vs_B_split: null  # do NOT choose the individual moduli`; the live incumbent build ships exactly the forbidden proxy 0.50, k_linc=1e2, and the three chosen moduli 15/15/150.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/cell/compartments.py:101-119 `NUCLEUS_DEFAULTS = dict(r_eq_um=5.0, …, k_chrom=15.0, k_lamin_b=15.0, k_lamin_ac=150.0, knee_strain=0.10, eps_rupture=0.50, kappa_ne=0.0856, k_vol=1.0e3, k_linc=1.0e2, …)` consumed at compartments.py:489 `p = {**NUCLEUS_DEFAULTS, **(params or {})}`; the forbidding yaml rows are ac/nucleus/params_i0b2.yaml:83-89, 143-152, 183-192. `with_nucleus: bool = True` (assemble.py:229) so this is the default build.

claims.claim: The claim that no nucleus GAP magnitude enters the resting force balance is refuted for the envelope bending rigidity: κ_ne = 0.0856 pN·µm is labelled TEST, yet the nucleus node-block carries a non-zero GATE-A residual of 0.1606 — 76% of the 0.21 gate and the largest of the three blocks. A TEST-labelled magnitude is therefore load-bearing for the GATE-A pass margin.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/cell/compartments.py:111 `kappa_ne=0.0856,   # envelope bending rigidity [pN·µm] (~20 kBT) — TEST`; the 'none enters the RESTING result' claim is ac/cell/compartments.py:25-32 docstring; the measured residual is docs/v2_audit/GATE_A_RESTING_CONVERGENCE_2026-07-23.md:37 `| nucleus | 0.1606 | 0.1606 | **PASS** |` and :128 'cortex 0.036, membrane 0.077, nucleus 0.16'.

claims.claim: The PI's own 2026-07-21 NM2B-pure baseline decision was never landed in code, and four of its values are still at the retired NM2A/AFINES numbers — including one the yaml itself calls a MISLABEL. `params_i0b3.yaml` records L_bb=0.323 (Melli2018, KB verdict OK), N_side≈14/side ≈28 heads (Nagy2013, OK, 'retire AFINES-10'), k_off0=0.4/s detachment '(NOT the 0.35 ADP-release) … fixes the mislabel below', d_step≈6 nm 'retire 11 nm muscle value'. Live code: L_bb=0.301, N_side=10, k_off0=0.35.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/motor/params_i0b3.yaml:35-41 (`selected_sources_pending_audit`) vs ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:142-153 `NMII_N_SIDE = 10`, `NMII_L_BB_UM = 0.301`, `NMII_KOFF0 = 0.35`; the still-live 0.35 row is params_i0b3.yaml:266-276 sourced to 'Stam-Hocky 2015 / Tam 2021'.

claims.claim: The same physical quantity — per-head crossbridge stiffness — carries two live values 1000× apart. `ac/cell` + engine use 1.0e3 pN/µm; `ff/hand_kmc.py` NMIIA still ships `link_k=1.0`, the surrogate that params_i0b3.yaml explicitly calls BROKEN ('at 1 pN/um the F_stall~0.5-2 pN strain is ~0.5-2 um, larger than the whole minifilament -> stall geometry collapses'). That preset is not dead code: it is the motor hand for the CORTEX, STRESS_FIBER and lamellipodium architecture rows and for the ac/weave SF regions.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ff/hand_kmc.py:124-126 `NMIIA_MYOSIN = HandParams(… v_max_um_s=0.2, f_stall=0.5, link_k=1.0)`; the 'broken' verdict is ac/motor/params_i0b3.yaml:151-156; consumers: ff/architecture_spec.py:93 `motor=MotorSpec(hand=NMIIA_MYOSIN, mode="bipolar", …)`, :154 (STRESS_FIBER), ac/weave/regions.py:99-105 `_sf_arch(... motor=MotorSpec(hand=NMIIA_MYOSIN, mode="sarcomeric", …))`. Also `ff/gamma_floor.py:38`, `ff/gamma_floor_dynamic.py:42,88`, `ff/network_warp.py:1822`.

claims.claim: Two more same-quantity splits in live code: unloaded stepping velocity v0 = 0.12 µm/s in `ac/cell` vs v_max = 0.2 µm/s in `ff/hand_kmc`; and the force-velocity FORM itself differs — `ac/cell`/engine use a Hill hyperbola with κ=0.5 while `ff/hand_kmc.active_step` is the linear κ→∞ law. This is a model-level inconsistency, not only a number.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:150 `NMII_V0_TEST = 0.12` vs ff/hand_kmc.py:126 `v_max_um_s=0.2`; ff/hand_kmc.py:106-117 `active_step … fac = 1.0 - f/self.f_stall` (linear, no curvature) vs assemble.py:151 `NMII_KAPPA_TEST = 0.5` fed to the Hill kernel. The unreconciled three-way κ conflict is documented at params_i0b3.yaml:119-142.

claims.claim: PI-GAP card S1 declares the SF axial stiffness EA_actin 'NOT FOUND — no sourced actin single-filament EA … NOT in corpus', and `build_sf_mechanics_topology` raises without it — but the sourced value is already in-tree with a KB citation verdict of OK. This over-declared gap is needlessly blocking the SF component's native magnitude gate; for seg=0.5 µm it yields k_axial = 4.4e4/0.5 = 8.8e4 pN/µm by the derivation the code already documents.
claims.evidence: Card text: docs/v2_audit/PI_GAP_EVIDENCE_CARDS_2026-07-25.md:312. In-tree value: ffn_sim/ff/kim_network.py:35 `EA_ACTIN_PN = 4.4e4            # pN  (Kojima 1994; actin axial stretching modulus)`; also ff/architecture_spec.py:157 notes 'EA=4.37e-8 N (Kojima 1994)'. KB: `select citation_key, verdict from source_audit` → ('Kojima1994_PNAS', 'OK'); references/SE_REGISTRATION_CANDIDATES_2026-06-09_sf-mechanics.md:17 records verdict 'OK (3-0)'. The blocking guard is ac/engine/sf_mechanics.py:281-283.

claims.claim: PI-GAP card F2 and `params_i0b4.yaml` both declare fascin inter-filament spacing `null / GAP — PI`, but the engine already carries it as a sourced constant with the primary DOI. The yaml gate register and the engine disagree about whether the same quantity is a gap.
claims.evidence: Gap declaration: ffn_sim/ac/weave/params_i0b4.yaml:124-133 `fascin_spacing_um: value: null … evidence_status: "GAP — PI"`, echoed at docs/v2_audit/PI_GAP_EVIDENCE_CARDS_2026-07-25.md:202. Sourced in code: ac/engine/protrusion.py:269 `FASCIN_INTERFILAMENT_SPACING_UM = 0.008   # ~8 nm, Courson & Rock 2010 JBC 10.1074/jbc.M110.123117` (+ :270 axial repeat 0.036).

claims.claim: The ONLY constants the lamellipodium declares GROUNDED and 'NOT gaps' — the Arp2/3 branch angle θ₀=70°, σ_θ=9°, and the equipartition-derived k_θ=0.173 — cite a KB source whose citation-audit verdict is DOI_DEAD, not OK. The code goes further and forbids any other value ('any other value is a magic-number substitution and is rejected at construction'), so a dead-DOI citation is load-bearing for a hard rejection rule.
claims.evidence: KB query on ffn_sim/outputs/tag_kb/kb.duckdb: `('Fassler2020_EMBOJ', 'DOI_DEAD')`. Declarations: ac/weave/params_i0b4.yaml:47-60 `evidence_status: "verified/High" … source: "Faessler 2020 EMBO J 39:e104254"`; ac/engine/protrusion.py:256-262 'These are the ONLY admissible branch-angle constants'; PI-GAP card §5 preamble line 232 asserts they 'are already GROUNDED — Faessler 2020 — and are NOT gaps'. CLAUDE.md citation-integrity rule requires verdict OK before citing.

claims.claim: Multiple constants that are live in code or are the recommended leads in the PI-GAP cards trace to KB sources whose audit verdict is not OK: Billington2013 = CHECK (L_bb=0.301 in assemble.py:144, and the N_side 28–30 claim), Freedman2017 = CHECK and Tam2021 = CHECK and StamAlbertsGardelMunro2015 = CHECK (f_stall=0.5 and k_off0=0.35), Veigel2003 = CHECK (x_β=0.6 nm → f0≈7.13 pN, assemble.py:154), Hill1938 = CHECK (κ=0.25 claim), Alert2016 = CHECK (the recommended ERM ρ₀≈100/µm²), Tseng2004 = CHECK (η_nuc), Block2018 = CHECK (IF crossover lead), Dejardin2020 = DOI_MISMATCH (the '8 pN LINC resting tension' the cards call sourced), Pereverzev2005 = NO_DOI_FOUND (the catch-slip law form used for filamin, the FA clutch, and the NMII CATCH_SLIP default).
claims.evidence: KB query on ffn_sim/outputs/tag_kb/kb.duckdb source_audit (551 rows; OK 313 / CHECK 167 / NO_DOI_FOUND 49 / DOI_MISMATCH 15 / DOI_DEAD 7): ('Billington2013','CHECK'), ('Freedman2017_BiophysicalJournal','CHECK'), ('Tam2021_Jour','CHECK'), ('StamAlbertsGardelMunro2015','CHECK'), ('Veigel2003','CHECK'), ('Hill1938','CHECK'), ('Alert2016','CHECK'), ('Tseng2004','CHECK'), ('Block2018','CHECK'), ('Dejardin2020','DOI_MISMATCH'), ('Pereverzev2005_BiophysJ','NO_DOI_FOUND'). Code sites: assemble.py:144,149,153,154; PI_GAP_EVIDENCE_CARDS_2026-07-25.md:290,321.

claims.claim: Eight sources cited directly in live code (or as the card's recommended proxy) have NO source_audit row at all — worse than a CHECK verdict, since nothing has been audited: Rusan 2001 (the MT DI proxy), Courson & Rock 2010 (fascin geometry, wired), Qin 2009 (IF_VIMENTIN_WALL_EA_PN = 13000 pN, wired), Lichtenstern 2012 (IF_LP_KERATIN_UM = 0.30, wired), Lin 2010 (IF_LP_VIMENTIN_UM = 0.50, wired), Jung 2011 (the L_p 1e-12 anchor), Morone 2006 (the 50–100 nm cortical mesh the seg_um recommendation rests on), Lorenz 2019/2023 (the keratin EA lead).
claims.evidence: KB query on kb.duckdb returned `[]` for each of rusan|courson|qin|lichtenstern|lin2010|jung|morone|lorenz|kreplak|forsting|norstrom|niederman|takatsuki. Live code sites: ac/engine/microtubule_rig.py:617-632 (Rusan), ac/engine/protrusion.py:269 (Courson), ac/engine/intermediate_filament_rig.py:63-73 (Lichtenstern/Lin/Qin/Block/Forsting), ac/fluid/params_i0b1.yaml:145 (Jung 2011), docs/v2_audit/PARAM_PROVENANCE_AUDIT_2026-07-24.md row 2 (Morone).

claims.claim: The three CONVENIENCE values that the companion provenance audit ranks as WORSE than the already-caught `density_per_fil` — cortex `seg_um = 0.5` µm (5–10× coarser than the sourced 50–100 nm mesh, zero KB rows), `length_um = 3.0` µm (3–30× too long, formin-only ⇒ no Arp2/3 short-filament population), and `density_per_fil = 20.0` — appear NOWHERE in the PI-GAP evidence-card inventory or in the handoff's PI-decision queue, and are plain silent defaults with no guard. The self-inconsistency the audit flagged is confirmed in code: the density is justified as DERIVED from FILAMIN spacing (L/δ_filamin = 3.0 µm/150 nm) while the crosslinker hand actually built is α-ACTININ.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:183-185 `cortex_seg_um: float = 0.5` / `cortex_length_um: float = 3.0` / `cortex_density_per_fil: float = 20.0`; ff/architecture_spec.py:88-92 `FilamentSpec(nucleator="formin", length_um=3.0, seg_um=0.5, …)` + `CrosslinkerSpec(hand=ALPHA_ACTININ, …, density_per_fil=20.0)` with notes ':91-97' 'crosslinks/filament=20 DERIVED … L/δ_filamin = 3.0µm / 150nm, filamin being the main cortical crosslinker'. The ranking is docs/v2_audit/PARAM_PROVENANCE_AUDIT_2026-07-24.md:19-32 and rows 2-4; absent from PI_GAP_EVIDENCE_CARDS_2026-07-25.md and from SUCCESSOR_HANDOFF_TO_OPUS5_2026-07-25.md:42-52.

claims.claim: The mixed formin+Arp2/3 cortex ships three 'FLAGGED modeling choice — a PI A/B/C decision' magnitudes as ordinary numeric defaults rather than None-gated slots, so the moment the fraction is raised above zero the un-decided values apply silently.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:194-198 `cortex_arp23_fraction: float = 0.0` / `cortex_arp23_length_um: float = 0.15    # representative SHORT Arp2/3 filament length [µm] (0.1–0.2; PI A/B/C)` / `cortex_arp23_seg_um: float = 0.05` / `cortex_arp23_mother_fraction: float = 0.2`; the flag text is the comment block at :189-193 'The Arp2/3 length/seg + mother fraction are FLAGGED modeling choices (a "PI A/B/C" decision — a sourced OPTION, not a silent default)'.

claims.claim: MT count per cell is a silent default of 40 in the compartment builder while the module docstring concedes it is 'a provisional geometry, not a sourced production count' against a proxy band of ~250–600 MTs/epithelial cell — i.e. the default is ~6–15× below the proxy order and enters the whole-cell unique-ID/population budget.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/solid/microtubule.py:104 `def build_microtubule_compartment(*, centre=(0.0,0.0,0.0), n_mt: int = 40, …)`; docstring ac/solid/microtubule.py:28-31 'GAP (surface to PI, never tuned): the MT COUNT per MCF7 cell is MCF7-absent — proxy ~250–600 MTs/epithelial cell (order-of-magnitude); ``n_mt`` here is a provisional geometry, not a sourced production count.'

claims.claim: Discipline is inconsistent inside the single top-level composed-cell native script: the SF axial stiffness is `required=True` on the CLI, but the NMII MASTER FORCE KNOB silently falls back to the GAP constant when the flag is omitted.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_composed_native.py:117 `ap.add_argument("--k-axial", type=float, required=True, …)` vs :158 `k_xb = float(args.k_xb) if args.k_xb is not None else float(NMII_K_XB_TEST)`. Same pattern at scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:421 `ap.add_argument("--k-xb", type=float, default=NMII_K_XB_TEST, …)`.

claims.claim: The NMII backbone persistence length is correctly source-gated to None in CellConfig, but the GATE-B native run supplied a diagnostic fixture and self-labelled it as non-production — so the banked GATE-B dynamic result includes a GAP magnitude filled by a sweep fixture, not a physiological value.
claims.evidence: Guard: ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:270-272 `nmii_backbone_lp_um: float | None = None` + `nmii_backbone_lp_source: str = ""`; fixture constant assemble.py:172 `NMII_BACKBONE_LP_DIAGNOSTIC_UM = 1.0  # convergence-sweep fixture only; never a production/runtime default`; the GATE-B caller sets `nmii_backbone_lp_source="MECHANISM_DEMO_DIAGNOSTIC_L_p_FIXTURE_NOT_PRODUCTION_PI_GAP"` at scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:475.

claims.claim: Membrane hydraulic conductivity L_p disagrees by ~62.5× between the code surface and its own parameter gate AFTER unit conversion (1e-12 m/(s·Pa) = 1e-6 µm/(s·Pa) vs code 1.6e-8 µm/(s·Pa)); the sourced MCF7 value is the yaml's. Still unfixed, PI-owned. Inert at rest, load-bearing for any bleb/osmotic/spreading dynamics.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:133 `L_P = 1.6e-8              # membrane hydraulic conductivity [µm/(s·Pa)] (gamma_floor code value; draft/MCF7)` and ac/cell/ng4_payload.py:53; vs ac/fluid/params_i0b1.yaml:139-149 `value: 1.0e-12 … unit: "m/(s*Pa)" … note: "Reconcile against code value 1.6e-8 (gamma_floor)"`. Arithmetic confirmed in docs/v2_audit/PARAM_INCONSISTENCY_RECONCILE_2026-07-24.md §2.

claims.claim: The same physical quantity — MCF7 resting cortical tension — is encoded twice at inconsistent values: `ff/gamma_estimator.py:41` carries the sourced Hosseini band MCF7_IQR_PN_UM = (180, 400) pN/µm, while `assemble.py:128` Π₀ = 40 Pa implies γ_total = ΔP·R/2 = 150 pN/µm — below the bottom of that same band held in the same repo. The turgor baseline and the tension acceptance band therefore cannot both be satisfied.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ff/gamma_estimator.py:41 `MCF7_IQR_PN_UM = (180.0, 400.0)        # MCF7 interphase SUSPENDED, Hosseini 2020 (0.18–0.40 mN/m)`; :42 `ACTIVE_FRACTION = 0.70`; vs ac/cell/assemble.py:128 `PI_0_PA = 40.0`. Cross-checked in docs/v2_audit/RESTING_SETPOINT_SOURCING_2026-07-23.md 'CORRECTED decision E' and TURGOR_PRESSURE_MCF7_2026-07-24.md §3 (40 Pa ⇒ 0.15 mN/m, below the whole MCF7 IQR).

claims.claim: Minor same-quantity split: F-actin steric diameter is 7 nm in the steric constant and 8 nm in the engine unit module. result.dimension: Component ownership + evidence-ladder reality (13 declared components of ac/engine)
result.summary: The 13-component / 32-connector registry in `ac/engine/contracts.py` is real, internally validated, and exact-once dispatch-covered — but that coverage is a *type-level* manifest, not a runtime. All eight canonical dispatch facades (`SurfaceBody`, `FluidCore`, `StressFiberActor`, `MicrotubuleRig`, `IntermediateFilamentRig`, `ProtrusionActors`, `NMIIActuator`, `ECMWorld`) are instantiated **only in tests**; every native driver bypasses them with per-slice owner classes, and the one "composed native cell" substitutes `_NativeMechanicsFacade` for all eight while no-op'ing five. Judged by executable evidence, only four components have a state owner that launches Warp kernels over arrays it holds: `nmii` (private force array, aliased positions, native head population), `ecm` (genuinely private device SoA, but 200 fibers and **zero crosslink bonds**), `sf_arc` (private arrays, 20 fibers — self-declared "NOT the native SF inventory"), and `cytosol` (borrowed `FieldGrid`). `cortex` and `membrane` — the two largest components — are `SurfaceComponentStateOwner`s with `_NoOpSurfaceMechanics` that **both alias the same `cell.pos_d`/`cell.f_d`**; their physics never left feature-frozen `ac/cell/driver.py`, and the real `CortexFilamentMechanics` delegate that `INTEGRATION_surface_body.md` labels KERNEL_BOUND is never constructed. `microtubule`, `intermediate_filament`, `lamellipodium`, `filopodium` exist only as owner classes exercised with `_FakeArray(is_cuda=True)` doubles — their `@wp.kernel`s have never been compiled, let alone launched. `focal_adhesion` has no owner class at all and `world_boundary` is bound as a bare `object()` because the `assert_fully_bound` guard demands nothing of a non-geometric, non-evolving component. Finally, the composed native "step" contains **no integrator** — `solve_candidate` zeroes forces, accumulates once, and returns — so the flagship "FIRST composed native cell" commit (whose own message says "NOT yet native-run") is a force-assembly pass wearing the vocabulary of a physical step.

claims.claim: All eight canonical dispatch facades that the exact-once manifest names as owners of the 13 components / 32 connectors are instantiated ONLY in test files. No production, script, or native-driver path ever constructs SurfaceBody, FluidCore, StressFiberActor, MicrotubuleRig, IntermediateFilamentRig, ProtrusionActors, NMIIActuator, or ECMWorld. The facade layer is a type registry, not a runtime.

Composed native lane: no inner mechanical solve/integrator, no GlobalCellLedger, no physics-derived acceptance predicate, ECM transaction/ledger stubbed, five facades no-op'd, cortex census defaulting to 128 active, sf_arc at 20 fibers, ECM at 200 fibers, membrane at subdiv=6. None of it has run on CUDA.
Intra-component events: all 13 components are has_events=False, so cortex turnover/nucleation/severing, NMII assembly, MT catastrophe/rescue and IF turnover are outside the graph entirely.
CellState registries are empty, so no component's population or rate is sourced; every count in every gate is caller-chosen.

Population/no-double-count machinery (allocate/release/sever) is unexercised in production and the per-step disjointness assert is vacuous — it re-validates constant literal ID blocks and mixes filaments, collagen segments and minifilaments as one namespace.
strengths: The architecture registry itself is genuinely strong: `reference_cell_architecture()` validates 13/13 unique components and 32/32 unique connectors, rejects one-way loads (`bidirectional=False` raises), rejects kinetic connectors that do not commit-on-accept, rejects inter-component connectors with identical endpoints, and rejects remap/topology-lock without generation checks (contracts.py:96-119).

Exact-once dispatch is a real build-time invariant, not a comment: `CellCandidatePipeline.__post_init__` rejects duplicate component/connector claims, rejects the same runtime scheduled twice in one phase, and rejects incomplete coverage (dispatch.py:229-287); `validate_canonical_facade_claims` diffs the manifest against the architecture and names the missing/extra sets (dispatch.py:191-216).

Composite-joint deduplication is enforced structurally in two places: `CellActor.bind_connector` refuses two runtimes for one `mechanical_group` (actor.py:55-62) and `CellWorldTransaction` deduplicates by object identity so the FA series joint cannot become two springs (world.py:42-60).

The accepted-step predicate discipline is real: `CellWorldTransaction.finalize_candidate` launches both rollback and commit for every participant and never reads the predicate on the host (world.py:78-98); every restore kernel branches in-device on `accepted[0]` (e.g. composed_native.py:119-138, erm_cortex_connector.py:90-111).

`nmii` is a genuine, adversarially-verified state owner: `_validate_production_mechanics` hard-rejects aggregate/two-anchor substitutes and requires explicit Stam-Hocky backbone + individual heads (nmii_actuator.py:460-482), and the cortex-motor slice demonstrated on the full native 70,686 population that tension is zero with no bound head and emerges only from k_on binding events.

`ecm` is genuinely KERNEL_BOUND over private device state, with `_require_distinct_storage` anti-aliasing validation, on-device parameter derivation (no host readback), active-flag gating through zeroed parameters rather than host-sized launches, and post-commit parameter refresh keyed to `topology_epoch_d`.

The nmii_sf_motor slice is the one place split ownership is physically real (two never-merged position arrays), and its REPORT.md explicitly withdraws a previously reported 'T -> 1.92 pN PASS' as an unconverged transient and refuses to quote magnitudes at a 15.5% residual — exactly the behaviour the no-gate-loosening rule demands.

The project's own scoping docs are unusually honest and are the reason this audit could be precise: NATIVE_COMPOSITION_SCOPE_2026-07-25.md states the advanced components 'do NOT yet run together' and that the composed builder's only concrete caller 'feeds CPU census DOUBLES'; ROLLING_ROADMAP.md:110 labels the interior column 'an explicit scaffold, NOT a CONNECTED claim'; sf_mechanics.py:105-124 carries a per-edge honest binding status; sf_population.py:29-31 states its counts are not the native inventory.

REQUIRED-PARAM discipline is implemented, not just documented: ERM Bell constants, NMII k_on/f_stall/catch-slip, nucleus eps_rupt, SF k_axial and fascin k all raise rather than defaulting (erm_cortex_slice.py:104-109, cortex_motor_slice.py:160-176, interior_column_slice.py:137-143), and `DynamicInstabilityRateCard.ratified` defaults False so an unratified proxy cannot silently drive a run.

`CellState` structurally forbids the abstraction it exists to prevent: any Rate/Distribution whose target kind is force/tension/count/topology is rejected, and `assert_cellstate_writes_no_force` proves the instance holds no device array and exposes no force-writing setter (cell_state.py:41-76, 224-251).

result.summary: The `ac/cell` feature freeze (PI 2026-07-22, decision card `de0b6391`) is being honoured in letter for the *driver contract* but broken in substance: 22 commits and **4,532 insertions across 11 files including 6 brand-new modules** landed in `ac/cell` in the three days after the freeze, and at least four of them are unambiguously new biology (mixed formin+Arp2/3 cortex population, a new Arp2/3 angle-harmonic force term launched in `_accumulate_all`, a resting bound-myosin cortical-tension mechanism, and a 3-model ERM connector spectrum whose model 3 is an explicitly *mean-field* lumped bond density). Two of those additions are dead code (`erm_spectrum*.py` is wired into nothing but its own test), and one (`erm_tether.py` +145 lines of two-array Bell KMC) is new physics written *into* the frozen incumbent to serve `ac/engine` — which also makes the Card-5 stage-4 "block executable import of `ac/cell`" plan unexecutable, since `erm_cortex_slice.py:46` and `erm_cortex_connector.py:50` are the only two engine→cell imports and both point at exactly that file. On the doc side the SoT is internally contradictory and, more seriously, over-claims: `ROLLING_ROADMAP.md:7` headlines "✅ GATE A CLOSED" for a gate whose own source doc (`GATE_A_RESTING_CONVERGENCE_2026-07-23.md:313`) says the closure is "SURFACED to PI for ratification", whose closure was obtained by *redefining the baseline* (dropping the myosin seed), whose three ensemble numbers (0.1398/0.1416/0.1586) exist **only in two markdown files** with no committed artifact and no `REPORT.md` in `outputs/ac/gate_a/`, and which was measured on a ~500 nm cortex mesh that the project's own memo calls 10–16× coarser than native (the physiological 75 nm rung still sits at 0.28 > 0.21). `COMPONENT_BUILD_MATRIX.md` is frozen at 2026-07-22 and now contradicts the roadmap outright (collagen "modulus-band conflict open" vs "RESOLVED in-tree"), while three 2026-07-23 docs still advertise the retired "one PI-GAP closes the resting gate" framing with no supersession marker — a convention that exists in the repo but is used in only ~11 of 253 `v2_audit` docs.

Doc-to-commit traceability is real, not decorative.

Withdrawals are recorded rather than quietly deleted: the SF-motor tension result is explicitly retracted in both the roadmap (:105) and the closeout (outputs/ac/gate_b_sf_motor/REPORT.md:84 'That was an unconverged transient and is withdrawn'), and the roadmap actively warns against re-firing stale work items (:11 'do not re-fire it', :37 'do NOT re-queue').

The census-double render bridge labels itself honestly at the data layer: composed_world_v2.json carries `"evidence": "CENSUS-WIRED"` and a note that geometry and forces are SYNTHETIC, and ac_composed_world_dump.py:11-22 spells out REAL-vs-SYNTHETIC. The scope doc NATIVE_COMPOSITION_SCOPE_2026-07-25.md then names the double problem itself ('its only caller that supplies concrete objects feeds CPU census DOUBLES').

Post-freeze parameter work is provenance-disciplined: the NMII capture-radius retirement (assemble.py:155-163) carries its full source chain and explicitly distinguishes the physiological 0.210 µm reach from the deliberately loose 0.6 µm diagnostic knob, and every script that activates the resting-myosin seed passes a source string ending in `_TEST` rather than laundering a PI-GAP as sourced.
The engine→cell dependency surface is genuinely small and is kernel-level reuse (2 import sites, one target file), not a wholesale dependency on the incumbent's driver or assembly path.

result.dimension: GATE + NATIVE EVIDENCE LEDGER — what has actually been proven on the GPU, and at what population
result.summary: The ac/ engine's gate ledger has a structural hole: of the eight 2026-07-24/25 gates whose results are quoted as landed, exactly ONE (`nmii_sf_motor`) has a committed machine artifact (`outputs/ac/gate_b_sf_motor/{REPORT.md,*.json,*.log}`), and it is the one that REFUSES its magnitudes. Every other load-bearing number — GATE A's closure `max|PF|=0.1398` and its 3-seed ensemble, GATE B's `bound 0→85%` / `γ 0→3.7 pN/µm`, the fine-mesh `3.42→0.13/0.28` root-cause A/B, the Arp2/3 `7014→47.5` chain, the ERM preload tension — exists only as prose transcribed by hand from stdout: the producing scripts (`ac_gate_a_fq_coarse_test.py`, `ac_gate_a_pf_descent.py`, `ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py`, `ac_gate_b_sf_arc_native.py`, `ac_gate_b_erm_cortex_native.py`, `ac_cortex_mesh_ab.py`) contain no `json.dump`/file writer at all. The single committed GATE A figure hard-codes the raw `max|F|` numbers (5.79/7.90) that §9 later withdrew and was never refreshed after the closure. Population honesty is mixed: GATE B cortex and the interior column ARE at 70,686 filaments/494,802 nodes, but every SF and ECM "native" claim runs 40 hand-set SF fibers / 360 nodes / 16 minifilaments and 200 Mikado fibers, and the successor handoff's "first composed native cell … full native population" contradicts its own commit body ("NOT yet native-run"). Two specific over-claims are decisive: the roadmap calls γ=3.7 pN/µm "real power-stroke tension" when the only surviving dump shows `γ_source=0.0191` vs `γ_network=3.7043` (the power stroke is 0.5% of the quoted number, and the viewer banner discloses the split the prose hides); and the GATE B cortex slice force-accepts every step (`accepted_d = ones`, `--balance-gate` raises `SystemExit`) with 40 explicit inner iterations, so its "dynamic steady-state" is a plateau of an unconditionally-accepted, non-converged relax — the same condition that caused the SF gate to withdraw its numbers, but with no convergence diagnostic computed at all.

claims.claim: GATE A is declared CLOSED on max|PF|=0.1398 (3-seed ensemble 0.1398/0.1416/0.1586) but NO committed artifact contains any of those numbers. outputs/ac/gate_a/ holds exactly one file (figs/gate_a_closeout.png); the producing script has no artifact writer. The only committed numeric artifacts for the resting baseline are pre-fix and non-converged.

claims.claim: The roadmap presents GATE B's γ = 3.7 pN/µm as "real power-stroke tension", but the only surviving data record shows γ_source (the crossbridge/power-stroke family) = 0.0191 pN/µm and γ_network (passive actin + crosslink) = 3.7043 pN/µm — the active term is 0.5% of the quoted number, 195x smaller. The measurement partitions turgor-borne passive actin tension INTO the network term by construction, and no committed artifact records the t0 baseline needed to attribute the network rise to myosin.

claims.claim: The GATE B cortex slice's "dynamic steady-state" is produced with the acceptance predicate hard-wired to accept: `accepted_d = wp.array(np.ones(1))` is passed every step, the balance-gate alternative is unimplemented (`raise SystemExit`), and the inner mechanical solve is 40 iterations of `inner_solver="explicit"`. So bound%/γ/max|PF| "plateau" under unconditional acceptance of a non-converged candidate — the same condition the SF gate identified as disqualifying, here with no convergence diagnostic computed at all.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:494 `inner_solve = make_inner_solve(cell, n_inner=args.outer, reshape_every=20, inner_solver="explicit")` with `--outer` default 40 (:416); :505-509 `if args.balance_gate: raise SystemExit(...)`; :510 `accepted_ones = wp.array(np.ones(1, np.int32) ...)`; :515 `slc.step(cortex_relax, dt_phys=..., accepted_d=accepted_ones)  # force-accept: watch γ rise`; :47-50 docstring admits "FORCE-ACCEPT: the demo force-accepts every step ... so binding accumulates and the mechanism is visible". ROLLING_ROADMAP.md:63-64 states "the tensed cortex reaching a dynamic steady-state (bound/γ/max|PF| all plateau)" with no force-accept caveat.

claims.claim: The kink root-cause claim is two separable assertions with very different support. That the `overlap_free` relaxation causes the plateau is supported by one native A/B (3.42 -> 0.13). That the mechanism is a ~8 nm transverse WCA push at crosslink loci is supported ONLY by code reading, an arithmetic scaling table, and a spatial correlation — the audit measures no actual node deflections and says so. The roadmap's "mesh-independent ~8 nm transverse node push" restates the WCA cutoff envelope (7.86 nm) as a measured displacement; the audit's own arithmetic needs only ~3.3 nm.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/CORTEX_KINK_AUDIT_2026-07-25.md:4 "Scope: DIAGNOSTIC / read-only. No physics or runtime code changed. This doc is the only committed artifact"; :72-73 the push target "is a fixed physical distance: r_c = 2^(1/6)·0.007 = 7.86 nm"; :86 "δ needed for a 5° kink ... 3.3 nm (well inside the 7.86 nm WCA envelope)"; :106 "the kinks appear only after the relaxation moves nodes" (inferred from the A/B, not measured per node). Roadmap restatement: ROLLING_ROADMAP.md:23-24 "a mesh-independent ~8 nm transverse node push, invisible at 0.5 µm, a 5° kink at 75 nm". Note the project itself already fell into a spatial-correlation trap on this exact plateau (FINE_MESH_MULTIGRID_DESIGN_2026-07-24.md:467-472).

claims.claim: The roadmap headline states smooth arcs collapse the plateau "3.42 → 0.13 with the SAME solver", omitting that the same diagnostic run also disabled the excluded-volume force (--no-steric) and left ~64k t0 interpenetrations. The source doc flags this explicitly as diagnostic-not-production; the summary that will be read does not.

Also note the default validated span is not the shipped one: ac/cell/assemble.py:225 `cortex_overlap_span: int = 2` while the 0.28 result is at span 8.

result.dimension: CONNECTOR REALITY — the 32 declared connectors of ffn_sim/ac/engine/contracts.py
result.summary: All 32 connectors are declared in `reference_cell_architecture()` (contracts.py:252-451) and all 32 are "covered" by the exact-once dispatch manifest (dispatch.py:94-188), but the manifest only proves a *method name is callable* — it never proves a kernel exists. Runtime reality: 9 connectors have a real two-sided Warp force kernel (A), 4 have a real one-sided kernel (B), and 19 are DECLARED-ONLY — a `Protocol` plus test doubles, with no non-test implementation anywhere (D). Of the 9 force-real ones, only 5 runtime objects are ever instantiated outside `tests/` (ERM, the two NMII MOTOR edges, the SF internal arc joint, and the three fluid boundaries); `LincJointPopulation`, `LoadPathJointRuntime` (the FA series joint) and every ECM connector runtime are constructed *only in test files*. Exactly TWO connectors have ever launched a force kernel on CUDA at a physiological population: `nmii_cortex_motor` and `membrane_erm_cortex` — and in BOTH native drivers the two "never-merged owner arrays" are literally the SAME array (`cell.pos_d`/`cell.f_d`), i.e. co-location with a logical index split, which the project's own hard rule forbids as a connection. The composed world is the sharpest facade: `build_composed_cell_world(..., require_complete=True)` passes its "every component and connector bound with a full API" gate against pure no-op `_CensusRuntime`/`_FacadeSpy` doubles (ac_composed_world_dump.py:85-160), and in the only real-owner composed world (`composed_native.py`) 30 of the 32 connector dispatch claims are satisfied by code that never touches them — 19 via `_excluded_facade_noop` (`return None`, composed_native.py:284-291) and 11 via facade `run` closures that dispatch only component mechanics. The transaction discipline itself is genuinely clean: no host `bool()`/`.numpy()` read of the acceptance predicate anywhere in `transaction.py`/`world.py`, and every commit path I inspected is device-gated. The docs (ROLLING_ROADMAP.md:194-196, NATIVE_COMPOSITION_SCOPE_2026-07-25.md, SF_CONNECTOR_BINDING_STATUS) are unusually honest about most of this; the drift I found is localised (a "Only device work" docstring over a GPU→CPU roundtrip, and a "native-runs 40 steps" roadmap claim with no artifact).

claims.claim: GENUINE STRENGTH: the accepted-step transaction discipline holds under adversarial reading. `CellTransaction.step` and `CellWorldTransaction.finalize_candidate` launch BOTH rollback and commit every step and never read the predicate on the host; every commit/rollback kernel I inspected selects its branch in-device from `accepted[0]`. I found no connector that commits irreversible state outside an accepted-step transaction, and no `bool(accepted)`/`accepted.numpy()` anywhere in ac/ or scripts/ (the only predicate-adjacent host reads are the out-of-loop clock-index diagnostics and `ac/fluid/scheduler.py:279-308 readback()`, which is an explicitly documented post-loop boundary).
claims.evidence: transaction.py:119-154 (snapshot → propose → solve → ledger → `self.world.finalize_candidate(predicate, ...)` → `self.clock.advance(predicate, dt_phys)`, no host branch); world.py:86-98 "``accepted_d`` remains device-resident; this method must not call ``numpy()``, ``bool()``" followed by unconditional rollback-then-commit fan-out; device gating verified in erm_cortex_connector.py:90-111, composed_native.py:119-138, linc_connector.py:1061-1075, load_path.py:552-585; `rg 'bool\(accepted|accepted.*\.numpy\(\)' ffn_sim/ac ffn_sim/scripts` → no in-loop hits

claims.claim: GENUINE STRENGTH: `nmii_sf_motor` is the one connector whose native evidence matches its architectural claim — two genuinely separate device arrays, verified by printing the distinct pointers, with a real emergent-tension mechanism (heads 0→301/320 by k_on events, tension exactly 0 while unbound, tension exceeding any single head load, 100% inward FA reaction, and a rejected step bit-restoring the binding SoA AND both position arrays). It is honest about its limits: the JSON records `residual_over_tension ≈ 0.155`, so quantitative tension is withheld, and every parameter is labelled PI-GAP.
claims.evidence: scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:323-324 `print(f"[sf_motor GATE-B] SPLIT OWNERSHIP: sf pos ptr={sf_owner.position_d.ptr} vs nmii pos ptr={actuator.position_d.ptr} (two never-merged arrays)")`; outputs/ac/gate_b_sf_motor/sf_motor_native_gate.json `"rollback_detail": {"binding_soa_restored": true, "sf_position_bit_restored": true, "nmii_position_bit_restored": true, "clock_did_not_advance": true}`, `"residual_over_tension": 0.155…`, `"params_pi_gap": {…}`

open_gaps: 19 of 32 connectors (59%) are DECLARED-ONLY: a Protocol plus test doubles, with no runtime object anywhere in non-test code — the whole protrusion family (8), the three cytosol immersed transfers, sf_cortex_transient, if_sf_plectin, mt_sf_spectraplakin, mt_cortex_capture, ecm_crosslink, membrane_ecm_contact, and the lamellipodium/filopodium MOTOR edges.

No composed world has ever been stepped on CUDA. `build_native_composed_cell_world` (the 'FIRST composed native cell') has a gbook script and zero recorded runs; the census-double world is the only composed world with an artifact, and it launches nothing.

The 'two never-merged owner arrays' invariant is unproven natively for the two connectors that HAVE run at physiological population — both cortex-lane drivers alias `cell.pos_d`/`cell.f_d`. The split-ownership evidence exists only in CPU tests and in the reduced-population SF lane.

19 of 22 kinetic connectors have no accepted-step kinetics: three LINC edges raise NotImplementedError by design (source-gated rate cards), the FA clutch has a commit kernel with no hazard law (PI card A1), and dorsal_arc_crosslink / ecm_crosslink / all protrusion edges / two NMII edges have no commit path at all.

The interior fluid column's three connectors are participants that carry no force natively — the frozen incumbent driver owns the coupling. Turning them into real connectors is the PI-gated Card-5 driver seam.

`assert_fully_bound()` cannot distinguish a Warp-resident owner from a no-op stub: it checks only method-name callability. There is no build-time assertion that a bound connector owns a device array or launches a kernel, so 'production-complete' is satisfiable by doubles.

No adjoint-work closure test exists for the four one-sided connectors (the three pressure/flux boundaries and the ECM far-field anchor). Their Newton-3rd claim rests on the assertion that the field's own div(v_s) source term is the work-conjugate reaction; nothing measures it.

`NativeSurfaceCoreForces.accumulate_internal` has an authoritative GPU→CPU→GPU roundtrip inside the candidate force pass while its docstring claims 'Only device work' — currently masked by `NoOpSurfaceMechanics` in the native lane, but a latent I0-A violation the moment the nucleus force moves under the engine.

Every magnitude on every connector that has run is a flagged PI-GAP (k_axial=1000, k_xb=1000, f_stall=0.5, k_on=50, capture=0.21, ERM Bell rates, α2β1 catch-bond, nucleus I0-B2, Π₀/L_p). No connector closes a quantitative band.
strengths: The kernels that DO exist are real fine-grained mechanics, not lumped proxies. Verified two-sided scatters: `erm_bell_force_pair_kernel` (ac/cell/erm_tether.py:276-277, membrane −f / cortex +f), `crossbridge_segment_split_r0bind_kernel` (ac/motor/segment_motor.py:498-500, +f on head / −(1−t)f, −t·f on the two target nodes), `_segment_joint_force_kernel` (load_path.py:543-546, barycentric gather with transpose scatter into both actors), `_linc_pair_force_kernel` + `_linc_native_socket_scatter_kernel` (linc_connector.py:986-989, 1017-1019, segment (1−u,u) gather and triangle barycentric scatter using the same weights so nodal virtual work equals pair virtual work).

The accepted-step transaction is genuinely device-resident: no host `bool()`/`.numpy()` on the acceptance predicate anywhere in the hot loop, both branches launched every step, clock advance device-gated, and `assert_disjoint_populations` promoted from a viz-time check to a per-accepted-step invariant (transaction.py:119-154, world.py:86-98).

Source-gating is honoured rather than papered over: `SourceGatedLincKinetics.propose_candidate` raises rather than inventing a rate law (linc_connector.py:1253-1257); `CortexMotorParams` refuses to construct without k_on/catch-slip; `ErmCortexConnector.__init__` rejects any non-positive/None rate constant (erm_cortex_connector.py:174-177). This is the anti-magic-number rule actually enforced in code.

The composite FA joint deduplication is real and correctly guarded: `CellActor.bind_connector` rejects two different runtimes under one `mechanical_group` (actor.py:55-61), and `CellWorldTransaction` deduplicates by object identity so the α2β1 series joint can never become two springs (world.py:42-60).

Self-reporting is unusually honest. `SF_CONNECTOR_BINDING_STATUS` (sf_mechanics.py:105-122) labels sf_cortex_transient / if_sf_plectin / mt_sf_spectraplakin as SEAMED with the exact missing piece; ROLLING_ROADMAP.md:194-196 states 'every protocol/spy slot still requires a production Warp binding before KERNEL_BOUND evidence'; NATIVE_COMPOSITION_SCOPE_2026-07-25.md states outright that the only concrete caller of the composed builder 'feeds CPU census DOUBLES'; the census dump labels itself 'CENSUS-WIRED' with 'geometry + forces SYNTHETIC'. My adversarial reading mostly corroborated these docs rather than contradicting them.

The exact-once dispatch machinery itself is sound as far as it goes: `CellCandidatePipeline.__post_init__` rejects duplicate component/connector claims, duplicate (runtime, phase) scheduling, and incomplete coverage (dispatch.py:229-287) — a genuine guard against double-counting force once real runtimes arrive.

`nmii_sf_motor` is a model of what a CONNECTED connector should look like: physically separate arrays (pointer-verified), emergent-only tension, exact-zero force when unbound, inward traction, bit-exact reject restore of both position arrays, and an explicit withheld-magnitude verdict.

result.dimension: HARD-RULE COMPLIANCE — static audit of the non-negotiables across ffn_sim/ac/
result.summary: Two of the seven rules are genuinely clean and enforced by real tests: HOOMD appears nowhere in ac/ (155 files, 55,378 LOC, zero imports, zero dynamic-import machinery at all), and hard-coded CUDA ordinals are blocked by an actual repo-wide regex gate (test_foundation_static_contract.py:64-67). GPU-residency is the strongest area: ac/fluid/scheduler.py confines every host read to an explicit readback() and its multi-step run() loop is fully device-resident, and there is real native 70,686 evidence on disk of hot_loop_dtoh_copies=0 with a non-vacuous positive control. Everything else has material problems. The canonical engine layer contains an in-inner-loop host readback (fluid_core.py:945) that the team's own plan doc admits "would break I0-A"; the acceptance-predicate contract that the whole component/connector architecture rests on has NEVER run on CUDA — all five GATE-B native demos hard-code accepted_d = ones (force-accept) and GlobalCellLedger appears only in CPU tests with _FakeDevice doubles, so kinetic KMC commits land on admittedly unconverged steps (maxPF 30.5); assert_disjoint_populations is silently a no-op in three of five slices (population_ledgers defaults to ()), and where it does run natively the cortex ledger seeds only 128 active IDs against a block of [0, 70686), making the "populations_disjoint: True" census a token. The worst magic-number offenders are the 0.21 pN GATE-A acceptance threshold (no derivation anywhere in the repo, hand-copied as a bare literal into ≥8 scripts) and dt_mu = 0.1/kmax, whose bare 0.1 multiplies the inner-solve convergence criterion by 10× and makes the effective force gate an explicit function of the mesh. The ac/cell feature freeze (PI 2026-07-22, "no new biology") was breached by at least four post-freeze commits to assemble.py, including a whole new Arp2/3 filament population.

claims.claim: Rule 1 is factually satisfied — zero HOOMD imports and zero dynamic-import surface anywhere under ac/ — but the enforcing test is trivially evadable and would not catch a dynamic import written two obvious ways.
claims.evidence: `rg -n -i 'hoomd' ffn_sim/ac/` returns only docstring/comment mentions (e.g. ffn_sim/ac/motor/minifilament_topology.py:7 'ported read-only from archive/hoomd_legacy … NEVER executed'). `rg -n 'importlib|__import__|exec\(|eval\(' ffn_sim/ac/` returns NOTHING — no dynamic-import machinery exists at all. The test at ffn_sim/tests/ac/test_warp_only_contract.py:36-52 matches a dynamic import only when the callee is `ast.Name(id='__import__')` or `ast.Attribute(value=Name('importlib'), attr='import_module')` AND `node.args` is non-empty AND arg[0] is a literal str. Therefore `from importlib import import_module; import_module('hoomd')` (callee is a bare Name, not an Attribute), `il = importlib; il.import_module('hoomd')`, and `importlib.import_module(name='hoomd')` (keyword-only ⇒ `node.args` empty) all pass the test. Also: `pyproject.toml:29 testpaths = ["ffn_sim/tests/ac"]` only binds when no path arg is given, and ffn_sim/tests/test_h1_cross_links.py:29 / test_cell_compartment_forwarding.py:24 do import `ffn_sim.archive.hoomd_legacy.*`, so `pytest ffn_sim/tests` escapes the quarantine.

claims.claim: The CANONICAL engine layer contains an authoritative GPU→CPU roundtrip inside the per-iteration force-accumulation path — the nucleoplasm volume pressure is computed on the HOST — and the module docstring calls this backend 'the native-first authoritative backend' while the team's own plan doc admits routing the nucleus through it 'would break I0-A'.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/engine/fluid_core.py:944-947 inside `NativeSurfaceCoreForces.accumulate`: `volume = float(self._volume_d.numpy()[0])` then `p_vol = -c.k_vol_pn_per_um2 * (volume - c.reference_volume_um3) / c.reference_volume_um3` passed back as `wp.float64(p_vol)`. That method is reached per inner iteration: fluid_core.py:994 `self.forces.accumulate(...)` from `NativeCoreSurfaceStep.accumulate_internal`, and interior_column_slice.py:546-560 documents `accumulate()` as 'One coupled candidate-force pass the caller's inner solve invokes EACH ITERATION'. fluid_core.py:982 claims 'This is the native-first authoritative backend'. Contradicted by ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/cell_engine/INTERIOR_COLUMN_CONNECTED_PLAN_2026-07-25.md:35-36: 'routing nucleus through `NativeSurfaceCoreForces` would break I0-A (hot-loop host readback `float(_volume_d.numpy())`, `fluid_core.py:945`)'. Decisive contrast: the FROZEN incumbent already solved this correctly — ffn_sim/ac/cell/compartments.py:143-169 has `_nucleoplasm_pressure_kernel` + `nucleoplasm_volume_force_arr_kernel` with the comment 'keeps NG-6 zero-roundtrip: p_vol computed on device, never read to host inside the inner solve'. So the canonical layer REGRESSED relative to the layer it is replacing. Mitigation: `build_core_surface_owner` defaults `mechanics` to `NoOpSurfaceMechanics` (interior_column_slice.py:509-511), and `rg -n 'NativeSurfaceCoreForces' ffn_sim/` shows the class is constructed ONLY in ffn_sim/tests/ac/engine/test_fluid_core.py:709,802 — never in any script or production path.

claims.claim: The accepted-step transaction contract — 'connectors commit ONLY on an accepted physical step' — has never been exercised natively: all five GATE-B native demos hard-code the acceptance predicate to always-TRUE, so irreversible KMC/binding state is committed on steps the runs themselves report as unconverged.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:509 `accepted_ones = wp.array(np.ones(1, np.int32), ...)` → :515 `slc.step(cortex_relax, dt_phys=..., accepted_d=accepted_ones)  # force-accept: watch γ rise`; the real gate is explicitly REFUSED at :504-508 `if args.balance_gate: raise SystemExit('--balance-gate requires a GlobalCellLedger + tol_sq_d wired by the Lead …')`. Same pattern: ac_gate_b_erm_cortex_native.py:332,360; ac_gate_b_interior_column_native.py:288,303; ac_gate_b_composed_native.py:232-234; ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:385,389. Only sf_motor also drives a rejected predicate (ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:427 `rejected_d`). Consequence in the headline run: the cortex-motor loop commits Bell/catch-slip attach+detach every step at maxPF ≈ 30.5 pN, ~145× the 0.21 pN gate.

claims.claim: The device-resident force-balance acceptance gate — the mechanism that is supposed to DECIDE whether a step is physical — exists only as CPU-test code driven by fake-device doubles; it has zero CUDA execution and no declared production tolerance value anywhere in the repo.
claims.evidence: `rg -n 'make_global_cell_ledger|GlobalCellLedger' ffn_sim/ --glob '!*.md'` finds the class at ffn_sim/ac/engine/ledger.py:150 and its only instantiation sites at ffn_sim/tests/ac/engine/test_ledger.py:48-51 with `_FakeDevice` (test_ledger.py:32 `is_cuda: bool = True` — a spy, not a device). No script under ffn_sim/scripts/ ever constructs it (`rg -n 'GlobalCellLedger|tol_sq_d' ffn_sim/scripts/*.py` → only the SystemExit message at ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:506-507). The tolerance is correctly caller-supplied (ledger.py:329-334 `tol_sq_d: (1,) float64 device scalar … Supplied by the caller so no numerical tolerance is baked in`) but no caller anywhere supplies it, and `rg 'tol_sq'` over docs/v2_audit/cell_engine/ finds no declared value — so the acceptance contract has no number, pre-declared or otherwise.

claims.claim: Rule 7 fails on both halves: assert_disjoint_populations is opt-in and is NOT invoked in three of the five slice builders (including the two native GATE-B slices), and where it does run natively the cortex ledger is seeded with 128 token active IDs instead of the 70,686 real filaments, so the accepted-step no-double-count invariant is checked over a stand-in population.
claims.evidence: The call sites are correct in principle — ffn_sim/ac/engine/transaction.py:76 (build) and :154 (after every accepted step, comment 'accepted-step no-double-count invariant') — but BOTH are guarded `if self.population_ledgers:` and the field defaults to empty: transaction.py:65 `population_ledgers: tuple[PopulationLedger, ...] = ()`, cortex_motor_slice.py:801 `population_ledgers: tuple[Any, ...] = ()`, interior_column_slice.py:628 same, erm_cortex_slice.py:359 same. The native cortex-motor gate never passes them — ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:491-493 `build_cortex_motor_slice(actuator_state=..., port=..., params=..., base_seed=..., device=..., max_segment_length_um=...)` — so in the single native dynamic run the invariant NEVER EXECUTES. Where it does run: composed_native.py:566-567 `cortex_ledger = PopulationLedger('cortex', id_base=0, capacity=int(cortex_capacity))` / `cortex_ledger.seed_active(cortex_active_ids if cortex_active_ids is not None else range(0, 128))`, and ac_gate_b_composed_native.py:202 passes `cortex_capacity=int(args.cortex_filaments)` (default 70686, line 119) but NOT `cortex_active_ids` — so the emitted `population_census` reports cortex block [0, 70686) with active=128 (script lines 248-249), while :256 hard-codes `"populations_disjoint": True`. Separately, the ledger is pure host state (population.py:65-66 `_active: set[int]`, `_free: list[int]`) described as a 'host mirror of the device free-lists' (composed_native.py:565) although no device free-list exists (`rg 'free_list|free_d' ffn_sim/ac/engine/*.py` finds none), and population.py:93 `frozenset(self._active)` rebuilds an O(N) host set per ledger on every accepted step.

claims.claim: The 0.21 pN GATE-A projected-force acceptance threshold — the single most load-bearing gate in the project — has no derivation, source, or grid-invariance argument anywhere in the repository, and is replicated as a hand-copied bare literal across at least eight scripts with no single definition site.
claims.evidence: Bare literal occurrences: ffn_sim/scripts/ac_erm_schwarz_probe.py:33 `GATE = 0.21`, ac_gate_a_pretension.py:31 `GATE = 0.21`, ac_gate_a_figure.py:18, ac_fd_operator_viz.py:17, ac_erm_schwarz_viz.py:15, ac_gate_a_kxb_sensitivity.py:47 `"gate_pn": 0.21`, ac_resting_converge.py:40,57 `"gate_ok": r.residual_end < 0.21`, ac_straddle_capture_sweep.py:49 `over = int((am > 0.21).sum())`, ac_myosin_stacking_probe.py:60. Exhaustive search for a derivation found none: `grep -rn "0\.21" --include='*.md' --include='*.py' --include='*.yaml' ffn_sim/ | grep -iE 'deriv|sourc|kT|sqrt|definit|contract'` returns only unrelated hits (a 0.21 nm ERM σ_radial in H1_H5_H7_MANIFOLD_CONTACT_ARCHITECTURE_2026-06-07.md:120, a 0.21 F/F_stall ratio in CORTICAL_TENSION_TRIAGE_2026-06-03.md:76, a 0.21 kPa·s viscosity in a paper summary). Every GATE-A verdict is judged against it, e.g. ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:243-245 'cortex 0.036 / membrane 0.077 / nucleus 0.16, all < 0.21'.

claims.claim: dt_mu = 0.1/kmax is an undeclared safety factor that multiplies the inner-solve convergence criterion by 10× and makes the effective force-residual acceptance threshold an explicit function of the discretization and of whichever composed spring is stiffest — a gate-relevant, non-grid-invariant magic number.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:942-964: `# ── 6. CFL: kmax over every composed stiffness → dt_mu = 0.1/kmax` … `dt_mu = 0.1 / kmax`, with `kmax = max(kappa.max()/seg_mean**3, kxl.max(), steric, myo.cfl_stiffness, nucleus.kappa_tilde/ell**3, k_vol, k_linc, membrane.kappa_tilde/ell**3, gamma_mem, k_erm, PI_0_PA*ell)`. Mirrored on device at ffn_sim/ac/cell/inner_mechanics.py:265-267 `"""Set ``dt_mu=0.1/max(k_mech, |Delta p| ell)`` entirely on device."""` / `dt_mu[0] = wp.float64(0.1) / wp.max(mechanical_kmax, k_pressure)`. That dt_mu enters the CONVERGENCE TEST: inner_mechanics.py:294-296 `max_projected_force[0] * dt_mu[0] <= tolerance_um`, with `tolerance_um = sqrt(eps64) * cell.convergence_length_um` (driver.py:506,1026) and `convergence_length_um = seg_mean` (assemble.py:1077). So the effective gate is `max|PF| <= sqrt(eps)·ℓ_actin·kmax/0.1` — the bare 0.1 loosens it exactly 10×, and it scales with ℓ_actin (and with 1/ℓ³ whenever a bending term dominates kmax), so a 'converged' verdict is not comparable across meshes. The module docstring justifies sqrt(eps) as 'a derived numerical-resolution criterion, grid-invariant' (inner_mechanics.py:12-14) but never justifies the 0.1; git log -S confirms it has never been revisited (single commit 34a3890d). Compare the contrast case done RIGHT: ac_gate_b_sf_arc_native.py:71-77 derives `COURANT_TARGET = 0.5` from the explicit-Euler limit C<2 with a Gershgorin λ_max bound and states 'This is NOT a fitted constant'.

claims.claim: The ac/cell feature freeze (PI 2026-07-22, 'no new biology; only P0 blocker fixes, instrumentation, and parity work') was breached by at least four post-freeze commits that added new biology to ac/cell/assemble.py, most unambiguously an entire new Arp2/3 cortical filament population and its branch-angle force term.
claims.evidence: Freeze text: ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/AC_DECISION_CARDS_2026-07-22.md:92-95 'Card 5 … Now — feature freeze. `ac/cell` is incumbent/reference; **no new biology**. Only P0 blocker fixes, instrumentation, and parity work.' (doc landed in de0b6391, 2026-07-22). Post-freeze commits touching ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py: `72d675ef` (2026-07-24) 'mixed formin+Arp2/3 cortex population — the missing native architecture' (assemble.py +44) and `e2ddda48` (2026-07-24) 'wire Arp2/3 70deg branch-angle force into _accumulate_all' (assemble.py +28, driver.py +8) — a new filament population and a new force term, not a P0 fix; `9bb91e0a` (2026-07-23) 'resting bound-myosin cortical-tension MECHANISM (candidate 1)' (assemble.py +85, driver.py +21, new resting_balance_oracle.py +289); `03399e2e` (2026-07-23) 'NMII straddle placement (defect#3)' (assemble.py +127). The resulting new config surface is visible in the frozen module: assemble.py:202-205 `cortex_arp23_fraction/length_um/seg_um/mother_fraction`, :284-287 `resting_bound_myosin_*`, :274 `nmii_straddle_placement`.

claims.claim: The headline native GATE-B cortex-motor run (the 'γ emerges 0→4.39' evidence) builds its NMII backbone-bending physics from a constant whose own definition forbids exactly that use: 'convergence-sweep fixture only; never a production/runtime default'.
claims.evidence: Definition: ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:174 `NMII_BACKBONE_LP_DIAGNOSTIC_UM = 1.0  # convergence-sweep fixture only; never a production/runtime default`. Uses in the native run: ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:191 `bending = NMIIBendingStiffness(persistence_length_um=NMII_BACKBONE_LP_DIAGNOSTIC_UM, ...)` and :474 `nmii_backbone_lp_um=NMII_BACKBONE_LP_DIAGNOSTIC_UM,  # materialise F6 angle topology`. The F6 arm/backbone angle-harmonic stiffness is derived from Lp (nmii_actuator.py:800 `k_theta_backbone = (L_p·k_BT)/a`), so the emergent γ depends on it. The production path correctly refuses a default (assemble.py:280-283 `nmii_backbone_lp_um: float | None = None … production-form bending is opt-in and source-gated; ``None`` leaves the gap explicit instead of running the diagnostic sweep value`) — the gate script bypasses that guard.

claims.claim: In the only native dynamic composition, the NMII component and the cortex port are the SAME two Warp arrays (cell.pos_d / cell.f_d) owned by the frozen ac/cell driver — so the engine 'state-owner' owns no state — and this is the one composition path with no storage-exclusivity check, which every other engine module does have.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:197 `position_d=cell.pos_d,   # ALIAS the global array` (NMII actuator) and :230 `position_d=cell.pos_d, force_d=cell.f_d,   # ALIAS the global array` (cortex FilamentMotorPortView) — literally the same storage for both transaction sides. The docstring claims otherwise: cortex_motor_slice.py:20-21 'the split crossbridge force `+f` into the ``nmii``-owned head array and `−(1−t)f`/`−t·f` into the two cortex port nodes (Newton's 3rd law across two never-merged arrays)' and :36 'co-location is never a connection'. The only guard is a component-NAME check (cortex_motor_slice.py:465-468 `if port.component != component_b: raise ValueError(... co-location is never a connection ...)`) — nothing compares storage. Contrast: ffn_sim/ac/engine/stress_fiber.py:178 `if len({_storage_key(a) for a in all_arrays}) != len(all_arrays)`, linc_connector.py:553 and :710-716, surface_body.py:180, load_path.py:161 all DO enforce distinct device storage. Mitigating: the index ranges are disjoint (heads at ≥ n_actin) so there is no shared DOF/implicit weld, and the split scatter is momentum-conserving; but `_SliceMyosinAdapter` (script:237-247) monkey-patches `cell.myosin` and sets `segment_runtime = None` to stop the driver double-committing the KMC, which confirms ac/cell — not the engine — owns the arrays and the accumulation loop.

claims.claim: There is an authoritative-looking host readback inside the inner PCG iteration loop (a control-flow break read from a device flag). It is default-off and argued bit-identical, but the D2H static guard does not cover the function it lives in, and the test that 'verifies' it is a source-string grep.
claims.evidence: ffn_sim/ac/cell/implicit_mechanics.py:2078-2080, inside `for iteration in range(1, self.max_iterations + 1)`: `if self.cg_check_every and iteration % self.cg_check_every == 0:` / `if int(self.active.numpy()[0]) == 0:` / `break`. Default is off — implicit_mechanics.py:1469 `cg_check_every: int = 0` — and self-justified at :1483-1489 'A control-flow readback for loop termination, NOT an authoritative per-step physics roundtrip'. claims.claim: I found no instance of gate-loosening in the sense the rule targets (a threshold moved to make a measurement pass); the one commit that touched a verdict TIGHTENED it, and the one threshold change I checked was a documented grid-convergence result rather than a tolerance edit.
claims.evidence: Commit fc762243 'fix(ac/gate-b): CFL-stable sf_arc relax + divergence-aware verdict' replaced a FALSE PASS with a stricter one: 'The sf_arc native GATE-B demo's step-(4) explicit relax DIVERGED (max|F| → ~7.9e51 … ) yet still printed a success verdict … Fix the verdict: RELAXED requires a FINITE final residual STRICTLY below the perturbed max|F| (ratio<1); otherwise print "DIVERGED (CFL — reduce dt)" and exit non-zero … Never a false-positive PASS' — and it derived the new step rather than picking one (ac_gate_b_sf_arc_native.py:71-77 COURANT_TARGET with a Gershgorin bound). Commit ea0babc4 'config(ac): PI-ratify membrane_subdivisions=8 for the production RESTING baseline' changed the MESH, not the 0.21 threshold, and assemble.py:241-245 argues it as 'textbook GRID CONVERGENCE of the Helfrich/Young-Laplace residual (edge→0), NOT gate-loosening'. The roadmap states the norm explicitly (docs/v2_audit/cell_engine/ROLLING_ROADMAP.md:144 'A failed gate … never causes an inline tolerance change, parameter fit'). Caveat: the 0.21 threshold this discipline protects is itself unsourced (see gate-a-021-unsourced), so the discipline is being applied to an undeclared contract.

claims.claim: ac/engine is genuinely disciplined about magic numbers — nearly every physical literal carries a source or an explicit GAP marker, and several modules refuse to construct without one — which makes the ac/cell offenders above stand out as the exception rather than the pattern.
claims.evidence: Literal density in ffn_sim/ac/engine/*.py is low and each is annotated: sf_mechanics.py:39 '4.6e5 pN/µm (Ferrer 2008 PNAS AFM, PI-approved)'; ecm_mechanics.py:63,123 flags `E_fibril_Pa = 1.1e6` as 'GAP (… no inline DOI — ecm_library:114)' and :67 forbids the convenience default 5.0e4; intermediate_filament_rig.py:58 derives kBT '1.380649e-23 J/K · 310.15 K / 1e-18 ≈ 4.28e-3 … passes the Magic-Number Block'; protrusion.py:271 `FASCIN_K_CROSSLINK_PN_PER_UM: float | None = None   # NOT FOUND — PI-GAP slot, no default` with :330-333 raising if theta0/k_theta are off the sourced Faessler 2020 anchor and :567 raising on the unset fascin slot; nmii_actuator.py:800 derives both angle stiffnesses; sf_nmii_population.py:30 'GEOMETRY IS DERIVED, NEVER CHOSEN (Magic-Number Block). Nothing here picks a length.'; cell_state.py:64-66 rejects any value lacking KB provenance. Residual soft spot: `mg_omega: float = 0.8` (implicit_mechanics.py:1468) is an undeclared smoother factor, defensible only because the V-cycle is preconditioner-only.

open_gaps: The acceptance-predicate contract is entirely unproven on hardware: GlobalCellLedger.assemble_balance has never run on CUDA (only ffn_sim/tests/ac/engine/test_ledger.py with _FakeDevice), no caller anywhere supplies tol_sq_d, and no production force-balance tolerance value is declared in any doc. Until a native run gates on balance_ok_d instead of accepted_d = ones, no engine component has real CONNECTED evidence.

The 0.21 pN GATE-A threshold needs a derivation or a PI-signed contract value, and a single definition site. It is currently a bare literal duplicated across ≥8 scripts with no recorded provenance, and every GATE-A verdict in the docs is measured against it.

dt_mu = 0.1/kmax (ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:964, inner_mechanics.py:267) needs the 0.1 either derived from the explicit-Euler stability limit (as ac_gate_b_sf_arc_native.py:71-77 does for its own step) or removed from the convergence criterion, because it currently sets a 10× multiplier on the effective max|PF| gate and makes that gate mesh-dependent.

ffn_sim/ac/engine/fluid_core.py:945 must move p_vol onto the device (the frozen incumbent already has the kernel pair at ffn_sim/ac/cell/compartments.py:143-169) before NativeSurfaceCoreForces can be used by anything, and the docstring at fluid_core.py:982 claiming it is 'the native-first authoritative backend' should be corrected until then.

assert_disjoint_populations needs to be non-optional (or the slice builders need to require ledgers), and composed_native.py:567's fallback `range(0, 128)` needs to be removed so a native run cannot silently census 128 filaments against a 70,686 block. The ledger also needs a device-resident free-list, since the docstring at composed_native.py:565 calls it a 'host mirror of the device free-lists' and no device free-list exists.

The NMII actuator and cortex port share cell.pos_d / cell.f_d in the only native dynamic run; the engine needs the _storage_key exclusivity check it already applies in stress_fiber.py:178, linc_connector.py:553 and surface_body.py:180, plus component-owned arrays, before 'components own state' is true of that path.

REQUIRED-PARAM needs to require provenance (as ffn_sim/ac/engine/cell_state.py:63-67 already does) rather than only finiteness, otherwise a caller satisfies a KB/PI GAP with invented numbers — as ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:120 does with CATCH_SLIP_PROVISIONAL.

There is no executable physiological-baseline audit. Nothing checks that erm_radial_pairing, preload_erm_balance, membrane/nucleus subdivisions, cortex_seg_um/density, cortex_arp23_fraction, cortex_overlap_mode and the resting-myosin setpoint are at their sourced values for a production run; the CLI cannot even set erm_radial_pairing.

The ac/cell feature freeze needs either enforcement (a static test on the frozen surface) or a PI-signed set of exceptions covering the four post-freeze biology commits (72d675ef, e2ddda48, 9bb91e0a, 03399e2e).

The D2H static guard covers only 4 named functions (test_foundation_static_contract.py:33-37); it should cover the whole inner-solve call graph, which is how the CG-loop readback at implicit_mechanics.py:2079 got in unnoticed. The CPU-launch guard (line 70-79) should also scan ffn_sim/ac/, not only ffn_sim/tests/ac/.

The source-grep 'proofs' in test_fiber_arclength_vcycle.py:487-504 should be renamed or replaced with behavioural checks; as written they certify multigrid fixed-point equivalence and bit-identical dx by asserting comment strings exist.
strengths: HOOMD rule is factually airtight, not just tested: zero imports and, more convincingly, zero dynamic-import machinery anywhere in 155 files / 55,378 LOC (`rg 'importlib|__import__|exec\(|eval\(' ffn_sim/ac/` is empty), so there is nothing for a static test to miss.

Hard-coded CUDA ordinals are prevented by a real repo-wide regex gate (ffn_sim/tests/ac/cell/test_foundation_static_contract.py:64-67), and the native gates are statically forbidden from falling back to Warp-CPU (same file, lines 82-92). This is one of the few rules with genuine mechanical enforcement rather than convention.

The fluid scheduler is a model of the GPU-residency rule: every one of its 25 host reads sits in an explicit `readback()` (ffn_sim/ac/fluid/scheduler.py:278-308), `outer_step` and the multi-step `run` loop contain none, and scalars are retained by `wp.clone` (:354-355 'never a D2H read').

The NG-6 profiler gate is non-vacuous by construction — it requires hot DtoH == 0 AND a positive-control DtoH > 0 (ffn_sim/ac/cell/native_gates/ng2_ng3_ng6.py:1173, 1179-1180) — and there is real committed native evidence at the full 70,686 population (ffn_sim/outputs/ac/implicit/native70686_implicit_memcpy_profile.json: hot=0, positive_control=1).

The transaction core keeps the acceptance predicate device-resident with no host inspection: transaction.py, world.py and events.py contain no numpy()/bool() on the predicate, and rollback + commit both run with the device selecting (transaction.py:146-150).

ac/engine's no-magic-number discipline is real and consistently applied: sourced values carry DOIs (sf_mechanics.py:39 Ferrer 2008), unsourced ones are explicit null GAP slots that RAISE rather than default (protrusion.py:271, 567; intermediate_filament_rig.py:843), geometry is derived rather than chosen (sf_nmii_population.py:30), and cell_state.py:63-67 rejects any value without KB provenance.

The one commit that touched a gate verdict tightened it, converting a false PASS on a numerical blow-up into a hard DIVERGED failure, and derived the corrected timestep from a Gershgorin bound rather than picking a value (commit fc762243; ac_gate_b_sf_arc_native.py:71-77).

The engine's out-of-loop host helpers are individually labelled with the rule they must not break — e.g. cortex_motor_slice.py:673-680, erm_cortex_slice.py:340-346, interior_column_slice.py:602-608 all read 'must never be called inside the inner solve (I0-A: no authoritative GPU→CPU roundtrip in the hot loop)' — which made this audit's in-loop/out-of-loop distinction tractable and shows the rule is internalised even where it is not enforced.
